risks.note: BRSR Section A states 'The Company is in the business of manufacturing diesel engines and its entire sale to Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd. ("M&M") for fitment into "Swaraj" tractors being manufactured by M&M', and M&M holds 52.11%. The MD&A adds: 'As a supplier to M&M, your Company would be directly affected by factors impacting tractor industry.' Any change in M&M's sourcing, in-housing of engines, or Swaraj-brand volumes flows straight through to the Company, and the pricing of virtually all its revenue is set inside a related-party arrangement (FY 2025-26 transaction value with M&M of Rs. 2026.67 crores, stated to be at arm's length).
risks.risk: Total customer concentration - the entire output is sold to Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd., which is also the holding company

risks.note: Management explicitly flags 'the rain-dependent nature of our agriculture, Government policy on procurement, credit availability' as factors affecting it. Tractor demand is described as 'closely influenced by monsoon conditions, crop realizations, government interventions, and the pace of farm mechanization', and the industry outlook names 'climatic variability' as a structural challenge. Volumes are therefore outside management's control.
risks.risk: Dependence on a monsoon- and policy-driven agricultural cycle

risks.note: The domestic tractor industry crossed one million units for the first time in FY26 at 11,60,300 units, up 23%, and the Company's engine supply rose to 2,02,771 units from 1,68,820. Management itself states 'domestic volumes are expected to normalize following a record FY26', so the FY26 base embeds cyclical peak volumes that need not repeat.
risks.risk: High-base risk after a record FY26 - industry volumes expected to normalize

risks.note: Management lists 'commodity price trends' among the factors that would directly affect the Company, and the industry section names 'rising input costs' as a structural challenge. Material cost is 78.3% of net revenue from operations (previous year 78.9%), so a small unrecovered movement in input prices is material to profitability, particularly given a single-customer pricing structure.
risks.risk: Input-cost / commodity price exposure on a thin conversion margin

risks.note: 'New regulations for tractors' is listed by management as a direct risk factor, and the industry is described as 'undergoing gradual technological and regulatory transitions with... preparedness for evolving emission norms'. Emission-norm transitions force engine redesign and re-certification cost onto the engine supplier.
risks.risk: Regulatory and emission-norm changes for tractors

risks.note: The MD&A notes 'initial investments in alternative fuel and electric tractor platforms signal a long term shift towards sustainable mechanization'. The Company's business is 100% diesel engines and their components (NIC 29104), so a shift away from the diesel powertrain is an existential product risk rather than a mix risk.
risks.risk: Technology-transition risk to alternative fuel and electric tractor platforms

risks.note: BRSR Section A records one plant and one office, both national, with no international locations; markets served span 2 states; exports are Nil; and 100% of turnover comes from manufacturing of diesel engines and components. There is no product, site or geographic diversification to absorb a disruption at the Mohali works or in the domestic tractor cycle.

The only BRSR material issue classified as a 'Risk' (rather than an Opportunity) is 'Ethical behaviour, Governance and Compliance', with the rationale that 'Any non-compliance could lead to litigation and may also impact the brand reputation'. Mitigation cited is a code of conduct for directors and employees plus a whistle-blower policy covering directors, employees, vendors, suppliers and other stakeholders.
risks.risk: Ethical conduct, governance and compliance - flagged by the Company itself as a Risk in its BRSR materiality table

Tractor demand is described as 'closely influenced by monsoon conditions, crop realizations, government interventions, and the pace of farm mechanization', and the industry outlook names 'climatic variability' as a structural challenge. Volumes are therefore outside management's control.
- The domestic tractor industry crossed one million units for the first time in FY26 at 11,60,300 units, up 23%, and the Company's engine supply rose to 2,02,771 units from 1,68,820. Management itself states 'domestic volumes are expected to normalize following a record FY26', so the FY26 base embeds cyclical peak volumes that need not repeat.
- Management lists 'commodity price trends' among the factors that would directly affect the Company, and the industry section names 'rising input costs' as a structural challenge. Material cost is 78.3% of net revenue from operations (previous year 78.9%), so a small unrecovered movement in input prices is material to profitability, particularly given a single-customer pricing structure.
- 'New regulations for tractors' is listed by management as a direct risk factor, and the industry is described as 'undergoing gradual technological and regulatory transitions with... preparedness for evolving emission norms'. Emission-norm transitions force engine redesign and re-certification cost onto the engine supplier.
- The MD&A notes 'initial investments in alternative fuel and electric tractor platforms signal a long term shift towards sustainable mechanization'. The Company's business is 100% diesel engines and their components (NIC 29104), so a shift away from the diesel powertrain is an existential product risk rather than a mix risk.
- BRSR Section A records one plant and one office, both national, with no international locations; markets served span 2 states; exports are Nil; and 100% of turnover comes from manufacturing of diesel engines and components. There is no product, site or geographic diversification to absorb a disruption at the Mohali works or in the domestic tractor cycle.
- The only BRSR material issue classified as a 'Risk' (rather than an Opportunity) is 'Ethical behaviour, Governance and Compliance', with the rationale that 'Any non-compliance could lead to litigation and may also impact the brand reputation'. Mitigation cited is a code of conduct for directors and employees plus a whistle-blower policy covering directors, employees, vendors, suppliers and other stakeholders.

hero.oneLiner: Swaraj Engines Ltd is a single-customer diesel-engine maker supplying 20 HP to 65 HP engines exclusively to Mahindra & Mahindra for fitment into 'Swaraj' brand tractors, having cumulatively supplied 1.96 million engines since 1989-90.
